Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)

3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.

understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. ## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

# AGENTS.md — Semantica

Semantic-HTML-first CSS library. Plain, well-structured HTML looks polished with
**zero classes**; opt-in classes cover only patterns HTML has no element for.
Pure CSS, no runtime, no dependencies.

> This repo root **is** the Semantica project. Sibling subfolders
> (`video-compressor/`, `techstack-advisor/`, `clean-code-checker/`,
> `cost-time-estimator/`, `vuln-scanner/`) are **separate projects** with their
> own setups — don't pull them into Semantica's build or docs.

## Goals

1. **Classless by default** — correct semantic HTML renders well untouched.
2. **Opt-in, not opt-out** — components/utilities are added deliberately, never forced.
3. **Themeable from one place** — every value is a `--sui-*` custom property.
4. **Accessible & native-first** — real elements + ARIA; prefer Popover API, `<dialog>`, `<details>` over JS.
5. **Zero-dependency, zero build to consume** — ship one `.css` file.

## Structure

```
src/                 # source, one file per concern (edit here)
  reset.css          # @layer reset   — modern reset
  tokens.css         # @layer tokens  — --sui-* vars + light/dark themes
  base.css           # @layer base    — classless element styling
  forms.css          # @layer base    — classless form controls
  layout.css         # @layer layout  — landmarks + .container/.grid/.stack/...
  components.css      # @layer components — core: button/card/badge/callout/tabs/...
  navigation.css     # @layer components — pagination/breadcrumb/steps/toolbar
  overlays.css       # @layer components — menu(popover)/popover-card/drawer(dialog)
  feedback.css       # @layer components — toast/banner/empty/progress-bar/loading-bar
  data-display.css   # @layer components — table modifiers/stat/timeline/chip
  form-components.css # @layer components — field/input-group/search/segmented/rating
  media-content.css  # @layer components — avatar-group/accordion/divider/ratio/codeblock/prose/hero
  utilities.css      # @layer utilities — escape hatches
dist/                # BUILD OUTPUT — never hand-edit
  semantica.css      # bundle    (~110 KB)
  semantica.min.css  # minified  (~67 KB)
scripts/build.mjs    # zero-dep concat + minify; FILES[] sets order
index.html           # landing/overview showcase
components.html       # full component gallery (every component, live)
```

Cascade order is fixed by `dist`'s first line:
`@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;` — later layers win,
so utilities and components override base regardless of source order.

## Sections (component groups)

- **Core** (`components.css`) — `.button`(+`data-variant`/`-size`), `.card`, `.badge`, `.callout`, `[role=tablist]`, `.switch`, `.avatar`, `[data-tooltip]`, `.spinner`, `.skeleton`, `.button-group`.

- **Data** — `table[data-striped|data-compact|data-bordered]`, `.table-wrap`(`data-sticky`), `.stat`, `.timeline`, `.chip`/`.chips`.
- **Forms** — `.field`, `.input-group`, `.search`, `.segmented`, `.rating`.
- **Media/content** — `.avatar-group`, `.accordion`, `.divider`, `.ratio`, `.codeblock`, `.prose`, `.hero`.

- One kebab-case root class per component (`.stat`). Variants/sizes/states are **`data-*` attributes**, not extra classes (`.badge[data-variant="success"]`, `button[data-size="lg"]`).
- **Logical properties only**: `inline-size`/`block-size`, `margin-block`/`-inline`, `inset-*`, `border-inline-start`. No `width`/`left`/physical margins.

npm run serve    # static server for index.html / components.html
```

`src/*.css` to that array or it won't ship.** No bundler, no PostCSS.

1. Pick/extend the matching `src/*.css` (or add a file + register it in `build.mjs` `FILES`).
2. Follow the conventions above; reuse existing tokens.
3. Add a live example to `components.html`.
4. `npm run build`, then eyeball both pages in light + dark.

- [ ] Autoprefix / Lightning CSS pass for wider browser support (`color-mix`, `@layer`, anchor positioning fallbacks).
- [ ] Per-layer partial builds (e.g. `semantica.classless.css` without components).
- [ ] Theme presets beyond accent (radius/density/font scale) + a 2-line theme switcher recipe.
- [ ] Publish to npm; add a CDN usage snippet.
- [ ] Token reference page generated from `tokens.css`.

enhancement with fallbacks.

content.text:
## Semantica research findings

Repo is in good shape overall: `dist/` is byte-for-byte in sync with `src/` (rebuilt and diffed clean), every component the README/AGENTS.md advertises has matching CSS (checked all ~35 class names), and the dark-theme token system covers components consistently — no missing dark-mode styling found. Ranked contribution ideas:

**1. Print stylesheet — highest value, currently absent.**
Only styling for print is a `.no-print` utility (`src/utilities.css:109-111`). There's no `@media print` reset, so a dark-themed page (via OS preference or `data-theme="dark"`) prints with dark backgrounds, `box-shadow`s waste ink/toner, and nav/toast-region/buttons print as-is. Add a print block (new section in `src/utilities.css` or `src/base.css`) forcing light colors, stripping shadows/backgrounds/transitions, hiding `nav`/`.toast-region`/`.skip-link`/interactive chrome, and avoiding page breaks inside `.card`/`table`/`blockquote`. Squarely fits "semantic HTML just works" — print is a native browsing mode nobody's covering.

**2. Forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) support for custom controls.**
Checkboxes, radios, `.switch`, and `.rating` use `appearance: none` + SVG `background-image` checkmarks (`src/forms.css`, `src/components.css`, `src/form-components.css`). Under `forced-colors: active`, background images are suppressed, so checked/unchecked state becomes invisible. Add `@media (forced-colors: active) { appearance: auto; forced-color-adjust: auto; }` overrides. Directly contradicts the README's "Accessible by default" claim today.

**3. `--sui-text-subtle` contrast.**
`--sui-gray-400` (`#94a3b8`) on white is ~2.2:1, well under WCAG AA. Most uses are exempt (disabled/decorative), but `blockquote cite` (`src/base.css:148`) and placeholder text render real content at this ratio. One-line `tokens.css` fix.

**4. CI drift guard (smaller, optional).** No PR-time check that `npm run build` output matches committed `dist/`; only a push-to-main deploy workflow exists. A tiny `git diff --exit-code dist/` step after build would catch forgotten rebuilds — distinct from the roadmap's larger "regression checks" item.

Files: `src/utilities.css`, `src/forms.css`, `src/components.css`, `src/form-components.css`, `src/tokens.css`, `.github/workflows/`.
